Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Horizon Health Partners Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during the session, please press star then the 1 key on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then 2. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Horizon Health Partners' financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are Dr. Michael Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Medical Officer; Tom Hargrove, Chief Operating Officer; and Elena Vasquez, Chief Innovation Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Michael Reynolds.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the second quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network of 45 acute-care hospitals and 120 outpatient facilities across the Southeast and Midwest, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on six key aspects: the impact of value-based care contracts on reimbursement, initiatives to improve operating margin, trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, breakdown of revenue by service line, revenue per admission trends and drivers, and net patient revenue year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter.

These areas highlight our progress in navigating industry shifts while driving growth and profitability. In value-based care, we're seeing meaningful reimbursement uplift from our expanding contracts. Our margin improvement efforts are yielding steady gains through labor and supply chain discipline. Volume trends show outpatient acceleration offsetting inpatient softness. Revenue breakdown reflects strength in high-margin outpatient and behavioral health. Revenue per admission is climbing on better case mix and payer optimization. And net patient revenue posted solid growth both year-over-year and sequentially.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Lisa to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Michael. Good morning, everyone. As Michael mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for the second quarter was $2.62 billion, an increase of 8.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, and the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives.

Our operating expenses were $2.44 billion, representing 93.2% of net revenue and delivering a 6.8% operating margin, up 120 basis points year-over-year. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in labor productivity and supply chain optimization.

Net income for the quarter was $120 million, or $1.05 per diluted share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

To give you deeper insight into the six key aspects Michael highlighted, let me start with the impact of value-based care contracts on our reimbursement. As we pivot from traditional fee-for-service to outcome-driven models, these contracts are reshaping our payer mix and supporting sustainable margin expansion. Our exposure to value-based care stands at about 28% of net patient revenue, or $1.2 billion annually, up from 19% two years ago. This includes our participation in Medicare Shared Savings Program ACOs under Track 3 with full downside risk, CMS Bundled Payments for Care Improvement Advanced for lower extremity joint replacements and cardiac bundles, and commercial deals with payers like UnitedHealthcare's Optum Value Network and Anthem's episode payments. For comparison, peers like HCA Healthcare are at around 25%, and Universal Health Services at 22%. Our faster adoption aligns with CMS's goal of 100% alternative payment models by 2030.

On reimbursement, value-based care has provided a net positive 7.2% uplift in effective rates per case compared to fee-for-service. In fee-for-service, our average Medicare case mix index-adjusted reimbursement per discharge was $12,450 this quarter. In value-based arrangements, like our BPCI-A joint replacement bundle where we hit 92% of target prices, we achieved $14,200 per episode—a 14% premium—thanks to 90-day readmissions dropping 18% year-over-year to 4.2%, below the national CMS benchmark of 8.5%, and post-acute savings of 22% via preferred skilled nursing networks. In our ACOs, we generated $45 million in shared savings this quarter at a 4.1% savings rate, capturing 75% upside under Track 3, equating to about $340 per member per year in added revenue.

Of course, there are challenges with downside risk. In Midwest markets with 42% Medicare Advantage penetration versus 35% in the Southeast, one ACO underperformed on sepsis readmissions due to rural access issues, leading to a $12 million payment back to CMS and a 15 basis point hit to EBITDA margin. But we've countered this; in Florida markets like Tampa and Orlando, reimbursements grew 12% year-over-year, supported by social determinants interventions lifting HCAHPS to the 85th percentile.

Industry trends back this: post-COVID, value-based adoption is up 35% per Health Care Payment Learning & Action Network data. CMS's 2024 Physician Fee Schedule shifts another 8% to advanced APMs, with commercial payers like Blue Cross Blue Shield covering 40% of lives in ortho and oncology bundles. While fee-for-service faces 9% year-over-year case cost inflation per AHA, our value-based cohorts saw only 4% due to efficiencies.

We're enabling this with our Epic-integrated Care Coordination Platform using ClosedLoop.ai predictive analytics to flag high-risk discharges 72 hours early, cutting avoidable admissions 25%. Strata Decision Technology tracks bundle margins in real time, hitting 95% profitability versus the industry 82% per ECG Management Consultants. These cost $28 million in capex last year but deliver 3.8x ROI.

Strategically, we've added 15 hospitals to Humana's Medicare Advantage networks in Georgia and Kentucky, aiming for 35% mix by 2025. We cap downside at 10% in new contracts and leverage our 2,500-strong employed physician group for 95/100 MIPS scores, unlocking $18 million in incentives. We project 9-11% reimbursement growth from value-based care in fiscal 2024, adding 150-200 basis points to EBITDA margins.

Next, our initiatives to improve operating margin, a core part of our 2024-2026 plan. This quarter's consolidated margin hit 6.8%, up 120 basis points year-over-year and our sixth straight sequential gain, with trailing 12-month at 6.5%—at the high end versus peers, matching HCA's 7.2% and ahead of Tenet and Community Health Systems. We're targeting 9% by 2026, needing 100-150 basis points annually, and delivered 60 from operations this quarter.

Our four-pronged approach: labor productivity, supply chain, revenue cycle, and high-margin service growth.

On labor, 52% of costs and up from pre-pandemic due to 5-7% wage inflation, our CareFlow Optimization uses AI scheduling via ShiftWizard and Epic across 85% of hospitals, cutting overtime 22% and agency use to 7%. In Southeast clusters, nurse-to-patient ratios improved 15%. We capped agency at 1.5x base, grew our float pool to 2,500, saving $45 million annualized with Kronos forecasting. Retention bonuses tied to length-of-stay hit 88% retention versus industry 82%. Midwest union pressures were offset, improving labor per admission 4.2% and adding 80 basis points.

Supply chain, our $2.8 billion spend up 12% since 2021 from GLP-1 shortages, SupplySync with HealthTrust targets 5-7% cuts. We got 18% savings on ortho implants and stents, $28 million this quarter; standardized 75% formulary drugs via Epic AI, cutting pharmacy 14%; VMI pilots in 30 hospitals reduced stockouts 40% and write-offs $12 million. Southeast led at +80 basis points, dropping supply to 14.2% of revenue, +50 basis points overall.

Revenue cycle: RevMax brought days in A/R to 42, denials to 4.1%. Waystar and Change Healthcare AI prevented $65 million denials, 92% first-pass rate; Experian pre-clearance upped collections 18%; 3M analytics yielded 2.5% better outpatient rates. Cash hit $4.2 billion, up 8%, shifting commercial mix to 48%.

High-margin expansion: inpatient 8.2% margins, outpatient 12.5%. Ortho/cardio up 22%, CMI 1.92; 50 ASCs at 18% margins with da Vinci; LOS to 4.2 days via CarePort, readmissions down 15%. Southeast electives +50 basis points; +30 overall.

Q3 guidance 7.2-7.5% margins, full-year 7.0%, $450 million capex for Epic. Risks hedged, diversified footprint.

Turning to trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, this shift is reshaping acute care. Inpatient adjusted patient days fell 2.8% year-over-year to 1.42 million, with admissions down 3.1% to 285,000, CMI steady at 1.68. Medicare Advantage at 42% of Medicare lives pressured this, plus elective shift.

Outpatient registrations up 7.2% to 4.8 million, 68% of mix from 64%, with ASC cases +12%, HOPDs +9%. Revenue per encounter $1,450 on 3.1% OPPS update.

By line: ortho inpatient -8.5%, outpatient +15% with Mako; general surgery outpatient +11%; oncology infusions +10%.

Sunbelt (55% hospitals, Florida/Texas/Carolinas): inpatient flat/+1%, outpatient +9.5%. Northeast/Midwest: inpatient -5.1% from Medicaid shifts, outpatient +6% via telehealth at 22% post-acute.

Drivers: value-based bundles, robotics shortening LOS 0.8 days, CMS tailwinds. We're adding 15 ASCs with USPI, HealthBridge Connect for monitoring +20% chronic visits, RevCycleAI -15% denials. Expect inpatient +1%/-1% H2, outpatient 8-10%, +50-75 bps margins.

On breakdown of revenue by service line, total $2.62 billion up 8.2% YoY, 6.1% same-facility.

Inpatient: $1.18 billion, 45%, -1.5% same-facility. Admissions 128,000 flat, ALOS 4.7 days via MediCore Pathways. RPA $9,200; payer 52% Medicare. Southeast +2%, Midwest staffing hit. 35% Medicare in ACO REACH, $45 million savings.

Outpatient: $920 million, 35%, +14.2% YoY. Visits +16% to 2.1 million, CMI 1.85, per visit $440. ASCs $450 million +22%, 85,000 cases $5,300. Texas/Florida +$60 million. da Vinci in 40 ASCs +25% volumes, 32% margins; Nuance AI -15% no-shows.

ED/observation: $265 million, 10%, +4.1%. 1.05 million encounters +5%, per visit $250, acuity 68% ESI 3+. Denial 12%; three new freestandings +$12 million.

Behavioral: $135 million, 5%, +18%. Admissions +20% to 28,000, per admission $4,800. Pinnacle acquisition +$25 million; Southeast +22%, telepsych 25% margins.

Physician/ancillary: $122 million, 5%, +9%. Home health +12% episodes; $50 million lab automation.

Mix: outpatient to 35%, inpatient to 45%; per patient day $2,650 +7%, contribution 28.5% +210 bps. ASC builds, AI readmissions for 10-12% outpatient growth.

Revenue per admission trends: RPA $13,450, +5.8% YoY from $12,705; adjusted $12,820 +6.2%, compounding 7.1% past five quarters, ahead of HCA/Tenet.

CMI to 1.92 +2.8%, ortho 18% admissions $16,800 RPA, TAVR +22%, CDI with 3M +12% HCC capture +$450.

Payer: commercial to 37% +8% rates; Medicare $11,800; 340B +$120. Commercial $15,200 +7.5%.

Service intensity: ALOS 4.7, neuro/onc +5%; cardiology devices +15%.

Southeast $14,200 +7.2%, Midwest $12,100 +3.1%.

Epic +9% capture, AI coding for H2 lift; $250 million neuro/ortho capex, 10% accretion by 2025. Q2 guide 5.5-6.5%.

Finally, net patient revenue $2.48 billion, +8.2% YoY, +3.1% QoQ. Volumes +5.6%, CMI 1.68; commercial per case $18,450 +7.1%.

Deductions 42.3% -50 bps via Epic, DSO 45. Southeast +11.4%, Midwest +4.8%.

QoQ: outpatient +4.7%, per day $3,210 +2.9%; AI denials -22% flagged.

Bundled pilots 15% ortho 3-5% margins; five new ASCs. Q3 7-9%, full-year $9.9-10.1 billion +7.5-9%.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Raj Patel for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thank you, Lisa. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our value-based care program has shown promising results, with a 20% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform, which now supports 22% of post-acute visits and integrates predictive analytics for high-risk patients.

Following that, Tom will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Tom Hargrove:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including CareFlow Optimization for labor productivity and SupplySync for supply chain management, which have resulted in significant cost savings—over $45 million annualized from agency reductions and $28 million quarterly from purchasing.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Elena for an overview of our innovation efforts.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Tom. We are committed to driving innovation across our organization. We are investing in new technologies and partnerships to improve patient care, enhance efficiency, and create new revenue streams. Our current projects include the Epic-integrated Care Coordination Platform with ClosedLoop.ai and da Vinci Xi robotics expansions, which directly address challenges like readmissions and procedural acuity.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Michael.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you, Elena. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for questions. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the specific cost savings achieved through the implementation of CareFlow Optimization?

Tom Hargrove:
Good morning, John. Absolutely. CareFlow Optimization has been transformative for labor productivity. By deploying AI-powered scheduling with ShiftWizard and Epic modules across 85% of our facilities, we've reduced overtime by 22% and agency nurse utilization from 12% to 7% of total nursing hours. Our internal float pool expansion to 2,500 clinicians, capped agency premiums at 1.5x base rates, and integration with Kronos for demand forecasting delivered $45 million in annualized savings. In the Southeast, we improved peak-shift ratios by 15%, and retention hit 88% with LOS-tied bonuses. Overall, this improved labor expense per adjusted admission by 4.2%, contributing 80 basis points to margins despite wage pressures. We're seeing similar traction in Midwest union markets.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Johnson:
Thanks. What are your expectations for the impact of telehealth on your revenue and patient access?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Hi, Emily. Telehealth is a game-changer for us. Our platform, integrated into Epic MyChart with remote monitoring from partners like Medtronic and Philips, now handles 22% of post-acute visits and has driven a 20% increase in chronic care management encounters. On revenue, it supports outpatient growth at 7-10%, with higher per-encounter yields from follow-ups and bundles. Patient access has expanded, especially in rural Midwest areas, reducing readmissions 15-18% and aligning with value-based incentives— we've captured $45 million in ACO savings partly through this. Expect it to add 50-75 basis points to margins while improving HCAHPS scores.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Mike Lee:
Good morning. Can you provide more details on your plans for investing in new technologies and partnerships?

Elena Vasquez:
Good morning, Mike. We're allocating $450 million in capex this year, with a focus on digital and procedural tech. Key is our $250 million in da Vinci Xi and Mako robotics across 80 facilities and 40 ASCs, boosting ortho/cardio volumes 15-25% and margins to 18-32%. Partnerships like ClosedLoop.ai for predictive discharge analytics cut avoidable admissions 25%, and Strata for bundle tracking hits 95% profitability. We're expanding ASC JVs with USPI to 25, targeting high-margin GI/pain, and value-based pilots with Humana/UnitedHealthcare covering 15-35% of ortho/Medicare lives. ROI is strong at 3.8x, positioning RPA growth at 6-7% and VBC mix to 35% by 2025.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Kim with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Kim:
Thanks for taking my question. On the margin initiatives, how sustainable are the supply chain savings given inflation?

Lisa Chen:
Hi, David. Sustainability is baked in. SupplySync with HealthTrust secured 18% off-contract on implants/stents for $28 million quarterly savings, formulary standardization cut pharmacy 14%, and VMI pilots eliminated $12 million write-offs. We've hedged 60% of 2024 supplies against inflation, which hit 12% since 2021 but only 4% in VBC cohorts. Regional leaders like Southeast at +80 bps show scale; even California lags are improving. Paired with 340B optimization, this drops supply to 14.2% of revenue long-term, supporting our 9% margin target.

Dr. Michael Reynolds:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Horizon Health Partners Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
